title: Speaking Up: Who Is, and Who Isn't
body_text: I’d like to update the situation described in this post and its follow-up. The first is a look at just how the Trump administration is trying to destroy federally-funded research in the US as we know it and replace it with cronyism and worse, and the second is a rather urgent request for people to speak up about what a truly terrible idea this is. So, has that part happened? To an extent. The AAAS, to its credit, quickly came out strongly against the proposals. The ACS, on the other hand, has been exceptionally timid and mealy-mouthed in its statement, saying that they are “actively evaluating” them and is conducting a “comprehensive analysis”. The furthest they’re willing to go is saying that ‘We appreciate that the proposed rule is concerning in its size and scope”. But concerning for whom? Not them yet, apparently - not until the comprehensive review is finished, eh? The American Physical Society has been much better, as has the ASM and the Society for Neuroscience. The AACR sounds opposed, as well they should be, but hasn’t gotten around to telling its members to do anything about it yet, from what I can see. Meanwhile, if the American Society for Clinical Oncology has anything to say, I can’t even find it on their web site. But the American Heart Association has come out in opposition, as has the American Cancer Society. There are also table-pounding editorials at places like the NEJM, and the more of that, the better. The American Diabetes Association, though, has said nothing about the OMB proposals, but that makes sense, in a grim way: as you may have heard, the organization had police escort some of their own members out of a recent conference after they handed out copies of an editorial protesting the administration’s actions - an editorial already published by the ADA, mind you. The scientists ejected were threatened with arrest if they went back inside the building. This does not exactly cover the ADA with glory, as the organization slowly, painfully realized. But it seems that it might take a little bit longer to speak up about the dismantling of the entire foundation of academic science research in the US. My earlier post, and any of those “in opposition” links above, will tell you how to leave a comment of your own on the proposed changes. I’m glad to say that I made comment #3,233, and it’s now up to almost 37,500, with just under two weeks to go in the open comment period. Please do leave a message if you get a chance: widespread objections are important, and make it harder, politically, for the administration to do what it wants. Now let’s get to a group of people who (as far as I can tell) have said nothing at all. That would be the CEOs of the major biopharma companies. I have searched but so far found no public statements about the OMB’s proposed attack on US science funding, which on the face of it might seem a bit odd, since (1) the great majority of the employees at these companies came through that exact funding system at some point in their careers, and (2) since the industry depends on the basic science research funded this way to make its own advances in applied and clinical applications. Allow me to advance what seems to be the obvious reason for this silence: fear. I’m not saying that it’s completely irrational fear, either. These CEOs are often rather annoying people, but they are for the most part not stupid, and they have been reading the political situation. The Trump administration has been corrupting and obstructing the regulatory state apparatus in every direction it can think of, with an eye to using these agencies to reward their friends and punish their enemies. These seem to be the highest purposes they can imagine; they’re certainly acting that way. Now consider how biopharma companies are totally at the mercy of such regulation. Clinical trials and the marketing approvals that come from them are an absolutely crucial part of the entire industry, and the federal government has both hands around the process. All it would take is a twitch of a finger at the FDA (especially, but other agencies as well) to completely disrupt the business and the financial outlook of any given drug company. Put crudely, there is a regulatory shotgun aimed at every single company that is trying to get a drug on the market (or to get it to stay there), and the Trump administration is composed of people who would have no compunction whatsoever about pulling the trigger. So the CEOs have decided to lie very still and hope that no one notices them. But if Trump’s gaze does move across them, they smile and wave and try to look helpful and harmless. The risks seem too high to do otherwise, as degrading as this is. But will it work? Only so long as Trump and his creatures see a benefit in it. Remember, Donald Trump sells out everyone. Loyalty, like truth, is not a virtue that resides in him. What does reside therein is a yawning void that demands total fealty, endless praise, more and more fame, more and more money, more and more and more. It’s like standing next to the event horizon of a black hole. The moment that he feels that he could get more power, more money, more of whatever it is that his shriveled soul is seeking, he will turn on the drug industry the same way he turns on everyone else. So, C-suiters, that’s the real risk you’re running. I’m sure it’s uncomfortable to weigh that one next to the risks of incurring Trump’s wrath sooner, but the latter could very well be even worse if and when it arrives. And there’s another advantage to acting now: you won’t have to fawn over him, or over RFK Jr., or over any of those intolerable blowhards that have been installed at the relevant agencies. I would love to see the industry grow a spine here and raise its voice just a tiny bit. Am I expecting it to? Well, that’s another question entirely. But there’s still time to do the right thing. The Trump administration might just decide to come after you if you do, of course. But if you sit back and let these funding rules go through, you are most certainly blowing up the foundation on which the entire industry has been built. Think about it, won’t you? Just a little?
